$comment: Source of truth for the AI Literacy Universe. Edited by hand. `scripts/learn/generate-terms.mjs` walks this file one term at a time; `scripts/learn/validate-terms.mjs` checks every generated file against it. Merged entries (e.g. an id covering ReLU and sigmoid together) exist because teaching them apart would produce three near-identical pages; the aliases keep every surface form searchable.

categories.name: AI Foundations
categories.plain: The words people use before they use any of the others. What counts as artificial intelligence, what a model is, and why nobody agrees on the boundary.

categories.name: How Machines Learn
categories.plain: Learning from examples instead of following written rules: what goes in, what changes inside, and what comes out.

categories.name: Neural Networks
categories.plain: The layered arrangement of simple numerical steps that most modern AI is built from.

categories.name: How Models Improve
categories.plain: The machinery of getting less wrong: measuring error, working out which settings caused it, and nudging them.

categories.name: Model Quality and Evaluation
categories.plain: How anyone can tell whether a system actually works, and the many ways a good-looking score can mislead.

categories.name: Large Language Models
categories.plain: The systems behind chat assistants: how they read text, how they produce it, and what they cannot do.

categories.name: Transformers and Attention
categories.plain: The architecture that made modern language models possible, explained without the mathematics.

categories.name: Search, Embeddings and RAG
categories.plain: Finding the right passage by meaning rather than by matching words, and handing it to a model so the answer has a source.

categories.name: Training and Model Adaptation
categories.plain: The stages between a raw model and a usable one, and the several different things people mean by "training it on our data".

categories.name: AI Agents and Automation
categories.plain: Systems that do not just answer but act: calling tools, taking steps, and needing supervision.

categories.name: Generative Media
categories.plain: Producing images, audio, video and code, and the authenticity problems that follow.

categories.name: Computer Vision and Language Technology
categories.plain: Reading pictures and reading prose: the task-shaped words that predate the chatbot era and still describe most deployed systems.

categories.name: Data and Infrastructure
categories.plain: What models are built from and what they run on, including the parts that cost money and the parts that go stale.

categories.name: Responsible AI, Human Rights and Safety
categories.plain: Who is affected, who is accountable, and what has to stay a human decision.

categories.name: AI Security
categories.plain: The ways AI systems are attacked, and why an attack on a language model rarely looks like hacking.

categories.name: AI Governance and UN Terminology
categories.plain: The vocabulary of the rooms where AI rules get negotiated, and the UN machinery the timeline records.
